title: Leray transfers the base-change mate of a map of sheaf complexes
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ and projections $g_X:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], $Lh^*$ [def-pc-derived-pullback], $Rh_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and canonical adjunctions and base-change map $\beta:L g^*R f_*\to R f'_*L g_X^*$ [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. Write $G_Z=R\Gamma(Z,-)$ [def-pc-global-derived-rhom], $S_h$ for exact restriction of global scalars, $e_h:G_SRh_*\cong S_hG_T$ for the canonical Leray comparison [lem-pc-global-hom-adjunction], and $s:S_fS_{g_X}\cong S_gS_{f'}$ for the scalar-square identification [def-pc-global-hom-pullback-comparison]. If $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, $E'\in D(\mathcal O_{X'})$, and $a:L g_X^*E\to E'$ is any morphism, write $\operatorname{adj}_h$ for the Hom bijection from $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$. Then $$S_f\bigl(G_X(\operatorname{adj}_{g_X}(a));e_{g_X}(E')\bigr);s_{G_{X'}E'};S_g(e_{f'}^{-1}(E'))=e_f^{-1}(E);G_Y\bigl(\operatorname{adj}_g(\beta_E;Rf'_*(a))\bigr);e_g(Rf'_*E').$$ This is an identity for arbitrary sheaf complexes and maps; no internal-Hom or tensor-Hom input, and no isomorphism hypothesis on beta or a, is present.

proof.text: Expand adj_gX(a) as the gX unit followed by RgX_*(a). Naturality of each canonical Leray comparison moves a through the two scalar paths. It suffices to check the identity when a is the identity of LgX^*E.

Expand beta_E as the f' adjunction transpose of the pullback-composition comparison followed by LgX^* of the f counit. Transpose under g, then use counit naturality and the triangle identities of f and f'. This recovers the direct-image-composition form Rf_*(unit_gX,E) followed by the canonical identification Rf_*RgX_* = Rg_*Rf'_*. All comparisons are the mates of the same pinned pullback composition comparisons.

The Leray comparisons for the two composite direct images are unique right-derived comparisons extending the identity on underived global sections. On K-injective representatives their derived-unit equations agree; uniqueness therefore identifies the two composites. The restriction-of-global-scalars composition maps are the identity module maps, and their square identification is precisely s. Apply derived global sections to the preceding unit identity and use this identification. Finally restore a using the naturality from the first step.

theorem schemeGlobalSections_baseChange_mate
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (E' : schemeDerivedCategory (pullback f g))
    (a : (derivedPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj E ⟶ E') :
    (schemeGlobalScalarRestriction f).map
        ((schemeDerivedGlobalSections X).map
          ((schemeHomPullbackAdjunction (pullback.fst f g)).homEquiv _ _ a) ≫
          (schemeGlobalSectionsDirectImageIso (pullback.fst f g)).hom.app E') ≫
      (schemeGlobalScalarSquareIso f (pullback.snd f g) g (pullback.fst f g)
        pullback.condition).hom.app ((schemeDerivedGlobalSections (pullback f g)).obj E') ≫
      (schemeGlobalScalarRestriction g).map
        ((schemeGlobalSectionsDirectImageIso (pullback.snd f g)).inv.app E') =
    (schemeGlobalSectionsDirectImageIso f).inv.app E ≫
      (schemeDerivedGlobalSections Y).map
        ((schemeHomPullbackAdjunction g).homEquiv _ _
          (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f (pullback.snd f g) g (pullback.fst f g)
            pullback.condition E ≫
            (schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd f g)).map a)) ≫
      (schemeGlobalSectionsDirectImageIso g).hom.app
        ((schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd f g)).obj E')
